article_content: Sarah Richardson asserts her mother Lianne Smith should remain imprisoned for murdering half-siblings Rebecca (5) and Daniel (11 months). A Spanish court convicted Smith, 45, of the 2010 suffocation deaths at a Costa Brava hotel. This followed partner Martin Smith's arrest on child rape charges involving Richardson, then 15. The family had fled to Spain in 2007 after Richardson reported Martin's 11-year abuse. Forensic evidence later disproved Martin's biological relation to the victims. Post-extradition, Lianne killed the children, later blaming Richardson in correspondence. Martin Smith died by suicide in January 2010 while awaiting trial. The court imposed a 34-year sentence. Richardson, now a mother in Carlisle, preserves holiday photos of the victims as memorials. She states Lianne's incarceration ensures reflection on her crimes.

article_content: Applying 'night-time sunscreen' after sun exposure may reduce skin cancer risk, according to Yale University research. Scientists discovered that ultraviolet (UV) damage continues for hours after sunset due to melanin transferring absorbed energy to DNA in darkness. This process causes DNA deformation through cyclobutane dimer formation, similar to direct sun exposure. Experiments with human and mouse melanocytes revealed UV radiation triggers enzyme reactions producing superoxide and nitric oxide, which excite melanin electrons. While melanin absorbs sunlight energy, it later transfers this energy to DNA in the dark, causing prolonged damage. Melanin-deficient cells showed damage only during direct UV exposure. Researchers propose developing evening sunscreens with compounds like vitamin E to block energy transfer mechanisms. Prof. Douglas Brash noted: 'Current sunscreens are applied pre-exposure, but post-exposure protection could mitigate delayed damage.' The study, published in Science, highlights melanin's dual role in protection and harm. Independent coral research explores UV-blocking compounds for potential oral sunscreens, though unrelated to this study. Experts suggest improved daytime sunscreens should target UVB/UVA rays and post-exposure chemical reactions involving reactive oxygen species.

Pokusi s melanocitima (stanice koje proizvode pigment) pokazali su da UV zračenje potiče stvaranje superoksida i dušikova oksida, koji zatim pobuđuju elektrone u melaninu. Iako melanin upija sunčevu energiju, kasnije je prenosi na DNA uzrokujući produljena oštećenja. Kod stanica bez melanina, oštećenja su se javljala samo tijekom izravnog izlaganja. Istraživači predlažu razvoj večernjih krema sa vitaminom E koje blokiraju ovaj štetni proces. Prof. Douglas Brash istaknuo je: 'Trenutne kreme se nanose prije sunčanja, ali zaštita nakon izlaganja mogla bi spriječiti kasnija oštećenja.' Studija u časopisu Science naglašava dvostruku ulogu melanina - štiti kožu, ali i doprinosi oštećenjima. Zasebno, istraživanje koralja otkrilo je spojeve za oralnu zaštitu od UV zračenja, ali to nije povezano s Yaleovim nalazima. Stručnjaci savjetuju kreme koje djeluju i na UVA/UVB zrake i na kemijske reakcije koje traju nakon sunčanja.

article_content: Retail workers at JB Hi-Fi stores nationwide have turned product labeling into an art form of comedic expression. Customers frequently encounter unexpected commentary alongside electronics and media - from Star Wars parodies to cheeky takes on celebrity scandals. These handwritten quips, documented on the unofficial 'JB Hi-Fi Reviews' site, reveal a culture of workplace humor. One employee reimagined Yoda's iconic 'Star Wars' wisdom for Angry Birds: 'Fear breeds angry birds, anger breeds hate, hate breeds defeat.' Another drew parallels between cycling video game 'Le Tour De France' and real-world doping scandals, jokingly slapping it with an R-rating. The now-legendary Nickelback review allegedly cost its author their job, while a staffer warned Breaking Bad viewers to 'get addicted to the show, not methamphetamine.' The compilations showcase creative wordplay, including a Robin Thicke single review advising 'for Paula’s sake, skip this album,' a movie cover joke comparing 'Life of Pi' to Calvin and Hobbes comics, and a wrestling game endorsement for 'fans of sweaty male grappling.' Though not company-sanctioned, these viral snippets highlight retail workers' knack for finding humor in daily tasks.
